// Expected values for the miller's work (docs/rules/milling.md), captured from the original program in the emulator (ADR 0008):
// tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb goods with a finished mill (type 15, a small building) at a flag, reduced to the passes that
// matter. The building's flag pointer (+0xe, which its handler 0x42e2a0 keeps its grain request through) is set by hand, as a built site
// leaves it (0x43ef82). The verb also runs 0x44579c before the castle, as the player setup of a new game does, so the rank of the grain
// request starts from the original's word. A scenario starts with a "#" line that names its verb command; each line after it gives, for a
// pass, the 16 bytes of the miller (slot 3, s3=: a settler without a job that the castle makes the miller) where his node, state, or part
// of the work changed, the 18 bytes of the building (b=, its flag pointer left out) where they changed, the flag's byte 4 and goods bytes
// (g=) where they changed, the request words of the flag (req=, the bytes 0x42 to 0x45) where they changed, the castle's grain count
// (grain=) and flour count (flour=) where they changed, and the generator's words (rng=) as they stand. The puts of the command lay the
// grains on the places of the castle's flag (slot 1) or of another flag by hand. The flags are listed in the order the engine numbers them
// (by column). The scenario flag-full runs to the pass 1800: the miller waits at the door with the flour from the pass 1470 while eight
// stones lie on the flag from the pass 1400. The stones make the road busy, so a settler without a job of the castle (slot 2, s2=) takes
// the job 0 at the pass 1484 and enters the road as its second carrier at the pass 1519 (docs/rules/carriers.md, "A busy road"); the first
// place frees at 1588, and the miller steps out at 1685. Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.
